image.altEn: Spanish-language xkcd comic #419: Forks and Spoons

titleText.en: Their biggest mistake was bringing Rachael Ray and Emeril to tour the lab and sign off on the project. That's when Spielberg caught wind of it.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive leaves the title text empty. The official English text imagines celebrity cooks Rachael Ray and Emeril approving the hybrid project before Spielberg learns about it, extending the laboratory disaster with a Jurassic Park-style joke.

regions.labelEs: UNA CUCHARA CRUZADA CON UN TENEDOR ES UN CUCHADOR.

applications.exampleEs: UNA CUCHARA CRUZADA CON UN TENEDOR
applications.explanationEn: Una cuchara names the first item, cruzada presents the crossing as a completed description, and con un tenedor introduces the other item.
Cruzada follows cuchara and describes which kind of spoon is meant.
Cruzada ends in -a to match the feminine singular noun cuchara.
Es is a form of ser because it states what the item is.

regions.labelEs: NUESTRO LABORATORIO HA CRUZADO CON ÉXITO UN CUCHADOR CON UNA CUCHARA.

applications.explanationEn: Ha is the present helper for one lab, and cruzado is the unchanged completed-action form of cruzar.

applications.exampleEs: CRUZADO CON ÉXITO UN CUCHADOR CON UNA CUCHARA
applications.explanationEn: Cruzado supplies the crossing action, un cuchador names the first item, and con una cuchara introduces the other. Con éxito is intervening outcome information.
Con and éxito form the fixed phrase that describes the action's successful outcome.

regions.labelEs: CON SUS FONDOS, PODRÍAMOS PRODUCIR HÍBRIDOS EN PROPORCIONES CORRESPONDIENTES A CUALQUIER FRACCIÓN BINARIA.

applications.explanationEn: Podríamos keeps the full verb poder and adds -íamos to present a possible action rather than a firm fact.
Podríamos supplies the possible ability, while producir stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
Correspondientes follows proporciones and describes which proportions are meant.
Correspondientes ends in -es to match the plural noun proporciones; this adjective has the same form for masculine and feminine nouns.
Correspondientes matches the earlier plural proportions, a supplies the required link, and cualquier fracción binaria names the value being matched.
Cualquier comes before the singular noun fracción; binaria is its describing word.
Binaria follows fracción and identifies the kind of fraction.
Binaria ends in -a to match the feminine singular noun fracción.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that one plant, animal, or type is crossed with another?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of cruzar, name the first item, then use con before the other item.
cards.noteEn: Cruzar often means to cross a place. In breeding, it means to combine two varieties. Cruzar changes for the person and time, while con stays unchanged. When describing the result, the first item can come before a completed-action form, as in una planta cruzada con otra.

example.es: El agricultor cruzó una rosa blanca con una roja.
example.en: The farmer crossed a white rose with a red one.

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.noteEn: Cruzada is the completed-action form of cruzar used to describe one feminine item. In breeding, cruzar means to combine one variety with another.

example.es: Es una rosa cruzada con otra variedad.
example.en: It is a rose crossed with another variety.

cards.promptEs: ser para identidad · estar para ubicación
cards.questionEn: Which Spanish “to be” verb says what something is, and which says where it is?
cards.answerEn: Use ser for identity or a defining description; use estar for the location of a person or thing.
cards.noteEn: This contrast is not simply permanent versus temporary. Forms of ser such as soy and es identify or describe what something is. Forms of estar such as están normally locate people and things. Events are a common exception: Spanish uses ser to say where or when an event takes place.

example.es: El museo es famoso y está en Madrid.
example.en: The museum is famous and is in Madrid.

cards.noteEn: Cuchador is a playful blend of cuchara and tenedor for a utensil that combines features of both.

example.es: Llevé un cuchador para el picnic.
example.en: I brought a spork for the picnic.

cards.answerEn: Use he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, or han followed by the verb’s completed-action form.
cards.noteEn: These are forms of haber, the helper verb used here like English “have.” For most verbs, the completed-action form ends in -ado after an -ar verb and -ido after an -er or -ir verb. This form is called the past participle, and it does not change after haber. How often this tense is used instead of the simple past varies by region.
cards.questionEn: How do you say “have done,” as in “I have finished”?

cards.noteEn: Cruzado is the completed-action form of cruzar. After a form of haber, it reports a completed crossing and does not change to match the item that was crossed.

example.es: El equipo ha cruzado dos variedades.
example.en: The team has crossed two varieties.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something happens successfully?
cards.answerEn: Use con éxito after the action.
cards.noteEn: Éxito means success. Together with con, the fixed phrase describes a successful outcome, much like the English word “successfully.” It does not change for person or time.
Sus is used before plural things that are owned. It agrees with what is owned, not with the owner; with usted, it can mean formal “your.”
Fondos can mean money made available for a project or organization, not only physical bottoms or backgrounds.

cards.answerEn: we could (a possibility or tentative suggestion)
cards.noteEn: Podríamos is the “would/could” form of poder for “we.” Poder keeps its whole dictionary form and adds -íamos. It often makes a suggestion sound tentative rather than stating a firm plan.

cards.questionEn: How do you form a Spanish “would” verb such as “would forget”?
cards.answerEn: Keep the whole dictionary form and add a conditional ending such as -ía.
cards.noteEn: The same endings attach to verbs ending in -ar, -er, and -ir. The ending changes for the person: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, or -ían.

cards.promptEs: poder + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone can, could, or may do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of poder for the person and situation, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: Poder changes to forms such as puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, and pueden for present ability or possibility. Podría can present a possible or imagined option. The following action keeps its -ar, -er, or -ir ending.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something corresponds to or matches a particular item or value?
cards.answerEn: Use correspondiente, or correspondientes for more than one thing, followed by a.
cards.noteEn: Correspondiente changes only for number: correspondiente is singular and correspondientes is plural. The small linking word a stays before the item, category, or value that provides the match.

example.es: Busca el número correspondiente a tu mesa.
example.en: Find the number corresponding to your table.

cards.answerEn: to; required after correspondiente before what it matches
cards.noteEn: Correspondiente normally uses a before the item, value, or category that provides the match.

example.es: Busca la llave correspondiente a esta puerta.
example.en: Find the key corresponding to this door.

cards.questionEn: How do you say “any” before one singular thing?
cards.answerEn: Put cualquier before a singular noun: cualquier libro, cualquier opción.
cards.noteEn: A noun is a naming word such as libro or opción. Before a noun, cualquiera shortens to cualquier. The noun stays singular even when the meaning is any one out of many. The plus sign in the Spanish prompt means “followed by.”

cards.questionEn: What is a binary fraction, and why do values such as 1/2 or 3/4 fit?
cards.answerEn: A binary fraction has a denominator that is a power of two, such as 2, 4, 8, or 16.
cards.noteEn: The denominator is the bottom number in a fraction. Powers of two are made by repeatedly multiplying by two: 2, 4, 8, 16, and so on. That makes 1/2, 1/4, 3/4, and 7/8 binary fractions, while 1/3 is not.

example.es: La fracción tres octavos es binaria.
example.en: The fraction three eighths is binary.

cards.answerEn: binary; based on two possibilities (feminine singular)

cards.noteEn: Espectro can mean a continuous range, especially a range of wavelengths or frequencies. In other settings it can also mean a ghost, but that is not the sense taught here.

example.es: La luz ocupa una parte del espectro.
example.en: Light occupies one part of the spectrum.

cards.answerEn: you all are (informal plural, mainly in Spain)
cards.noteEn: Estáis is the present form of estar used with vosotros or vosotras when speaking informally to several people, mainly in Spain.

cards.answerEn: Use a form of estar followed by an action word ending in -ando or -iendo.
cards.noteEn: Estar changes to show who is doing the action: estoy, estás, está, and so on. For most verbs, replace -ar with -ando (hablar → hablando) and replace -er or -ir with -iendo (comer → comiendo, vivir → viviendo). This is similar to English “am/is/are doing.”
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone is in the middle of doing something?

cards.noteEn: Jugando is the form of jugar ending in -ando that presents play as ongoing. With danger, power, feelings, or another serious matter after con, it can mean toying with or handling it carelessly.

cards.questionEn: How do you warn that someone is toying with or taking risks with something serious?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of jugar followed by con and the risky thing.
cards.noteEn: Jugar con literally means to play with. With danger, feelings, power, or another serious matter, it means to toy with it, handle it carelessly, or take a risk. Jugar changes for the person and time; con stays unchanged.

example.en: The company is playing with fire.

cards.answerEn: what; that which (as part of lo que)
cards.noteEn: Lo combines with que to refer to an idea, action, or whole situation rather than a masculine noun. Together, lo que means “what” or “the thing that.”

cards.questionEn: How do you say “what” or “the thing that” without naming a specific object?
cards.answerEn: Use lo que to refer to an idea, action, situation, or unnamed thing.
cards.noteEn: Here lo is neutral: it does not stand for a masculine noun. Que introduces the information that identifies the idea or thing. Together they work as one unit.

example.en: I don't understand what you're saying.

cards.answerEn: what; that which (as part of lo que)
cards.noteEn: Here que completes lo que, a neutral expression meaning “what” or “the thing that.” It does not refer to a particular masculine or feminine noun.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something happens a stated amount of time later?
cards.answerEn: Put the length of time before después.
cards.noteEn: The duration comes first: tres días después means “three days later.” This differs from después de tres días, which presents the same duration after después and means “after three days.”

example.es: Tres días después, llegó la carta.
example.en: Three days later, the letter arrived.
